basis: Independently clear source analysis d89b70c5: narrow direct request/completion, actual CLI/localstdioMCP, own Session/durable identity/one dispatch/full capture, T070 views separate. Exact wire defined now before test sources; no product prototype.

entry.packet: Existing exact stride-poise/v1 schema/operation/input and strict UTF8 JSON/EOF; common Session/config/packet limits and errors unchanged.
entry.selection: Optional top-level commands selects this versioned config for these operations only. Other operations ignore commands, including malformed unused values. Missing selected commands is commands_not_configured/unavailable1/resultnull. Real prepared own Session required; Task/Stage/shared DB absent.

configuration.known_fields: Every shown known field required. Unknown options at any config object level are ignored and raw config bytes remain unchanged. No alias/default config, live config write or automatic repair. Schema exact; bool is not integer.
configuration.paths: request_store/output_root resolve from config parent using ordinary path resolution. Parent of request_store and output_root are operator-prepared existing directories. request_store differs from own Session store. output_root contains only per-execution generated child directories; explicit unique configured file names are leaf names. file_mode integer0..0777.
configuration.limits: id_bytes/poll_ms/capture_chunk_bytes/terminate_grace_ms/completion_budget_ms/delivery_margin_ms/transport_budget_ms/transport_margin_ms/mcp_max_message_bytes/mcp_max_messages are positive integers. sqlite_timeout_seconds finite number>=0, bool excluded. Grace is strictly less than request cleanup_budget_ms.
budget_relationships: At command.request admission only: completion_budget_ms >= execution_budget_ms + cleanup_budget_ms + delivery_margin_ms.
For each selected operation: transport_budget_ms >= completion_budget_ms + transport_margin_ms.
configuration.budgets: Selected host/CLI test wait must actually accommodate transport_budget_ms. Application does not enlarge values. Execution deadline begins at actual execution-owner start/spawn attempt and uses monotonic time; cleanup budget starts on natural exit/deadline/protocol completion and bounds its owned drain/reap. Completion waits separately on retained state; actual returned outcome, not a guessed fixed timeout signal, is recorded. Completion/delete have no new execution budget to admit. A separate completion caller may select a shorter positive wait budget against the same stores/Session; this changes only that read wait, not retained input/execution settings. Replaying command.request still compares its original selected execution settings.
configuration.initialization: Command owner normally creates its new catalog on first valid admission in the prepared parent. This is creation of a new own managed store, not repair/migration of existing data. Existing incompatible/invalid catalog returns explicit unavailable error without overwrite. Readers/absent deletes do not create a store. Exact private schema/normal preparation mechanism belongs to CODEdesign; it is not a test oracle.
configuration.metadata_bound: Execution replies have fixed metadata fields and at most two source references/full-result reference, bounded ID strings and native file paths. Arbitrary stdout/stderr/MCP response bodies are stored outside replies. T070 owns explicit minimal/range presentation budgets; no second internal clipper or premature minimal API is added here.
configuration.error_classification: Existing SQLite user_version other than the supported version => command_store_incompatible with that integer; malformed non-SQLite bytes => version:null. SQLite busy/locked => command_store_busy. Other SQLite opening/writing I/O => command_store_io errno:null unless an actual OS errno is exposed. No inferred errno from a SQLite numeric result code. Ordinary absent catalog read/delete does not initialize it.

command.request.command_id: Nonempty opaque UTF8 string without NUL, <=id_bytes in UTF8, preserved exactly; not a filesystem path. Scoped to own saved Session.
command.request.argv: Nonempty array of strings without NUL; argv[0] explicit absolute native executable path, subsequent empty strings valid. Exact list passed without shell interpolation.
command.request.cwd: Explicit nonempty absolute native directory path text without NUL. Actual unavailable cwd/executable produces a recorded not_started OS outcome, not a fabricated exit.
command.request.env: Full explicit string-to-string child environment, nonempty keys without NUL/=, values may be empty; no merge with caller environment.
command.request.mcp: command requires null. mcp_stdio requires exact {protocol_version,client_info,tool_name,arguments}; protocol_version/tool_name nonempty UTF8 strings without NUL; client_info exact {name,version} nonempty text, arguments JSON object.

command.completion.command_id: Same meaningful opaque own-Session identity; returns current retained result, waiting within completion budget for TERMINAL/UNKNOWN. It never creates a new execution.

command.delete.command_id: Explicit data retirement of own identity and its generated stdout/stderr/full-result files after readers/owned writer processes have finished. This is not cancellation or application self-repair.

managed_object_operations.owner: Command execution capability, composed with existing own Session and output-file owner; no Task or generic CRUD service.
managed_object_operations.create: First valid command.request atomically records exact input and selected execution settings, then dispatches once. Same identity/exact input returns existing retained snapshot with replayedtrue; different input returns command_reuse_conflict with no dispatch.
managed_object_operations.read: command.completion reads/waits on the same own identity. Terminal and known UNKNOWN snapshots retain actual output/response; repeat reads do not relaunch or edit input.
managed_object_operations.update: Caller editing of admitted input is unsupported, reusing the already accepted exact-input/replay decision. Observation updates belong only to actual execution owner. A new intended execution uses a fresh ID; no public command.update or generic update API.
managed_object_operations.delete: Explicit command.delete removes only selected own record/generated files, no root/foreign Session or independent command data. Missing/repeated delete succeeds with the same absent result. Proper-use precondition: complete/read result and finish its consumers, or independently stop the owned writer before retirement; this operation does not infer/kill processes or add global waiting/locks. Ordinary delete I/O failure retains the record until remaining owned cleanup succeeds and exposes actual error; retry continues same requested absence. Owned capture cleanup order is configured stdout, then stderr, then full result, then generated empty directory, and finally the record; already absent own paths are tolerated. Stop on the first actual I/O error and retain the record for retry; no receipt rewrite that invents successfully removed bytes.
managed_object_operations.retention: Execution identity/replay guarantee lasts while its record is retained. After disposal choose a fresh ID for a new intended execution; no hidden historical tombstone/archive service is introduced. This defines the new object lifecycle; no existing user data is deleted by designing or testing it.
managed_object_operations.equality: Compare complete admitted JSON input and selected execution settings with JSON types: null/bool/number/string/array/object distinct, bool true differs from number1. Object member order is irrelevant, array order/text/opaque data significant; JSON numbers1 and1.0 represent the same numeric value. Completion-only wait/transport budgets are not execution identity settings. No hash/digest admission.

metadata_response.termination: null until genuinely observed, else exact {kind:exit,exit_code:integer0..255}, {kind:signal,signal:positive integer}, or {kind:not_started}.
metadata_response.deadline_exceeded: Boolean true only when owner actually observes execution deadline before exit, including later exit0/exit7. Natural exit and timeout remain distinct.
metadata_response.business_error: null for CLI/before MCP call outcome; actual result.isErrorbool (absent means protocol false) determines true/false, explicit JSON-RPC error means true. Nonboolean isError is an invalid protocol response. Complete actual response stays in full_result; no body/summary inline.
metadata_response.source: stdout/stderr null before publication, else exact {source_id,path,bytes,complete}; opaque stable ID, absolute owner-generated path, integerbytes>=0, boolean complete. Full separate raw bytes including NUL/nonUTF8 preserved. A partial capture reports actual retained bytes and completefalse. T069does not add active-prefix range/minimal API.
metadata_response.full_result_ref: null before full result publication, else exact {path,bytes}; existing absolute file and actual UTF8 JSON byte count. No hash/signature/source-integrity admission.
metadata_response.error: null or exact {code,details,action} for known execution/protocol/capture uncertainty. Outer request/wait/storage errors have their existing envelope owner; child nonzero/observed timeout alone is an actual outcome, not a malformed packet.
metadata_response.replayed: true only for a repeated identical request; false for new request and completion reads. First admission may return ADMITTED/RUNNING or already observed final state; complete whole permitted snapshots are compared, not partial fields.
metadata_response.transient_snapshots: ADMITTED/RUNNING before final publication have termination:null, deadline_exceeded:false, business_error:null, stdout:null, stderr:null, full_result_ref:null,error:null. Execution-owner observations publish one complete final snapshot atomically; no intermediate partial-reference API. Thus an active completion wait expiry is compared as a whole RUNNING snapshot once child readiness is independently established.

full_result.fields: Same execution facts/sources as metadata, without operation/replayed/self-reference. mcp_response is null or the COMPLETE actual tools/call JSON-RPC response, including all result/error/unknown fields, not a filtered DTO. Both raw sources also remain complete/partial truthful as observed. Input/env secrets are not copied into the public full receipt; exact admitted input/config remains at the execution owner.
full_result.publication: Publish after actual capture/termination observation; retain exact own result. UNKNOWN can retain known child exit and complete raw sources while a requested MCP response/business effect is not established. No inference from PID absence/time alone, no automatic redispatch or configuration repair.

mcp_boundary.supported: Local Linux stdio with exact configured argv/cwd/full env. initialize(selected protocol/client_info), notifications/initialized, tools/call(selected tool_name/arguments); tool inventory discovery is not required by this execution API. Existing capability probe retains its own list/read_only semantics.
mcp_boundary.correlation: Validate JSON type as well as value of each response ID against the outstanding request; bool is not an integer RPC ID. A nonmatching ID is command_protocol_failed/invalid_response in the actual phase; it is never accepted as another result or silently consumed. Retain raw bytes, no second tools/call/dispatch.
mcp_boundary.capture: Store every actual received protocol byte and full stderr. Match peer-emitted raw bytes independently; preserve full tools/call response in result file. Correctly completed call result.isErrortrue is business_errortrue with actual server exit0, not a fabricated process failure.
mcp_boundary.errors: Valid JSON-RPC error retained completely and reported as mcp_response_error. EOF before requested tools/call response => UNKNOWN/command_observation_lost with actual termination/capture, no second call on repeat. Incompatible selected protocol => command_protocol_failed before tools/call. Proper-use configured protocol/message/budgets are explicit; no external host/network MCP availability claim.
mcp_boundary.full_response: mcp_response is the exact complete tools/call response frame, including jsonrpc/id and every result/error/unknown field; RPC IDs are field-scoped dynamic correlation values. Initialize/list/notification frames also remain in complete raw stdout; new execution uses direct tools/call without requiring discovery.
mcp_boundary.primary_source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/messages; requests have non-null string/integer IDs unique within this session, responses match ID and contain exactly one result/error, notifications have no id. Version2024-11-05 only, no optional-feature expansion.
mcp_boundary.notifications: A syntactically valid JSON-RPC notification without id may precede either response; count and retain it, then continue to the matched response. Ignore its optional method-specific semantics; this does not implement subscriptions/logging/progress APIs. A notification cannot satisfy a pending request. Invalid response/result/isError shape is invalid_response.
mcp_boundary.message_bytes: mcp_max_message_bytes counts raw UTF8 bytes of one incoming LF-delimited frame EXCLUDING its one LF delimiter. The positive bound is inclusive. Exceeding it or the count is command_protocol_failed/{phase:actual phase,reason:message_limit}. Output capture continues within cleanup to retain actual bytes, including offending input; rejected frame is not a matched mcp_response.
mcp_boundary.message_count: mcp_max_messages counts all complete incoming nonempty frames in this execution from initialize onward, including notifications and error/invalid frames; inclusive. Outgoing initialize/initialized/tools.call frames are NOT counted. Empty LF frame is invalid_response, not a free message. No counter reset between initialize and tools.call.
mcp_boundary.packet_limits: Existing shell packet_bytes bounds only caller input, never incoming peer frames or retained full MCP result. Fixed metadata excludes the full result; an admitted small request can produce a valid peer frame above packet_bytes within selected MCP limit.

outer_mapping.success: ok/exit0/errornull/evidence[] and complete metadata for ADMITTED/RUNNING or normally observed terminal result, including child nonzero and observed deadline. This means successful delivery of the recorded outcome, not command/business success.
outer_mapping.observed_execution_error: unavailable/exit1/full metadata result/error copied from metadata.error for not_started/protocol/capture failure or UNKNOWN; no child exit fabricated. MCP ordinary result.isErrortrue remains deliveredok0 with business_errortrue and exact full response.
outer_mapping.completion_expiry: unavailable/exit1/current metadata snapshot, outer command_wait_expired/{command_id,budget_ms}/wait:command; no mutation/relaunch or guessed exit, result.error preserves actual execution error rather than becoming wait failure. Stable supported budgets are sized to actual selected execution+cleanup; later same identity read continues.
outer_mapping.validation_order: Existing common config/strict outer JSON/packet/schema/operation first. Selected commands presence/known config/path/budget capacity then operation input shape/value, then actual own caller/prepared Session. New request requires open Session; existing reads/retirement may use its retained closed Session. Check stored exact identity/input before any new target effect. Config/shape/admission failure creates no command store/output/child.
outer_mapping.existing_session_errors: Retain existing actual Session errors and pointers. Missing own Session is existing session_not_found/unavailable1/resultnull/details{}/ensure:session. Closed new request is existing session_closed/rejected2/details{status:closed}/select:session; completion/delete may read the retained identity. Existing common errors are not redefined.

outer_errors.details: exact {path:<missing/known faulty field, or containing object for extra key>}
exact {schema:<unsupported string>} for request schema; nonstring is invalid_request /input/schema

exact {execution_budget_ms,cleanup_budget_ms,completion_budget_ms,delivery_margin_ms} when their inequality fails; grace>=cleanup is invalid_request /input/cleanup_budget_ms. transport inequality is invalid_config /commands/limits/transport_budget_ms

recorded_errors.details: exact {path:<actual OS error filename or requested executable>,errno:integer|null}
exact {phase:mcp_response|dispatch|execution|publication}; capture failures have command_capture_failed only

recorded_errors.state: TERMINAL when child termination known, otherwise UNKNOWN

lifecycle_limits: command.delete data retirement is used after result consumers and owned writer processes finish; it neither cancels nor waits on a live command. Proper use and operator procedures own that precondition; no process/race/tamper defense or global lock is invented. Ordinary file cleanup error leaves the record for explicit retry, reports actual path/errno and preserves truthful partial effects. No filesystem-wide rollback/selfrepair promise.
evolution: T068prospective outer gateway/hash/lock/revision/timestamp fields are superseded by this scoped direct contract after independent approval; no shipped command runtime/consumer exists. Exact selected versions are explicit, no aliases/dual formats. This is not a change to native Poise receipt/history integrity or unrelated apps.

termination_and_cleanup.execution_deadline: Observe child exit first on a ready cycle. If it is not observed before the monotonic execution deadline, set deadline_exceeded true and immediately SIGTERM the owned process group. Start the one cleanup budget then. At terminate_grace_ms after TERM, SIGKILL that group if termination/pipe completion is still outstanding. Do not invent the resulting signal: reap and retain actual exit or signal.
termination_and_cleanup.natural_exit: Natural direct-child exit starts the one cleanup budget for draining remaining inherited pipes; deadline_exceeded remains false. Drain EOF, no unbounded communicate/wait. A normal descendant can keep a pipe open beyond that budget; stop capture at the bound and publish its true partial bytes. No promise to supervise independent descendants forever.
termination_and_cleanup.mcp_finish: After matched tools/call result or known protocol rejection, close the server input and start the one cleanup budget for natural server termination and capture. Do not immediately signal a finite peer that can exit on EOF. Execution timeout still applies until this finish point. A peer that does not finish inside cleanup yields unknown actual termination; do not fabricate exit0.
termination_and_cleanup.no_extension: Cleanup starts once at the first qualifying execution deadline, observed direct-child exit or MCP protocol finish. Signals, errors and repeated completion reads never restart/extend it. Drain and reap share its bound.
termination_and_cleanup.capture_io: On real stream file write/open error, retain that error errno and actual saved prefix; continue draining/discarding unsavable bytes within the same execution/cleanup bounds so a finite producer can finish normally. Failed source complete:false even if its pipe later reaches EOF; other source complete reflects its own EOF/save status. Error priority if both streams fail is stdout then stderr.
termination_and_cleanup.exhaustion: At cleanup bound close remaining capture handles. Every source missing EOF or suffering save failure is complete:false. Any such stream has command_capture_failed with {stream:first stdout then stderr,errno:actual IO errno or null for drain exhaustion}; state TERMINAL if direct-child termination known, otherwise UNKNOWN; termination actual or null. If captures are complete but termination unobserved, state UNKNOWN/command_observation_lost phase:execution. command_observation_lost phase:capture is removed to avoid overlapping classifications.
termination_and_cleanup.precedence: Capture failure/exhaustion takes error precedence over protocol/business error; full actual matched mcp_response and known business_error are still retained. With complete capture and known termination, known protocol failure is TERMINAL/command_protocol_failed; matched RPC error is TERMINAL/mcp_response_error; EOF before matched call response is UNKNOWN/command_observation_lost phase:mcp_response. Child nonzero or deadline alone is not error. Every error/UNKNOWN response maps unavailable1; valid observed child timeout/exit maps ok0.
